methods.title: Host system wall clock
methods.source: Rust std::time::SystemTime on the host running hemant-shell
methods.uncertainty: unknown (synchronization source, offset and drift are not measured)
limitations: A point snapshot; its age grows after it is read.
Not verified: readable or agreeing with another clock is not verification.
Supported range 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 UTC; values before 1970 cannot come from the host clock.

methods.title: Cloudflare Workers wall clock
methods.source: Date.now() supplied by the Cloudflare Workers runtime; converted to integer nanoseconds with millisecond resolution
methods.output_units: integer nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC (Unix count; millisecond resolution)
methods.uncertainty: unknown (runtime clock synchronization source, offset and drift are not measured)
limitations: A point snapshot; its age grows after it is read.
Not verified: runtime clock may be readable without having known accuracy.
The source has millisecond resolution; lower decimal places are zero padding, not measured precision.
Leap seconds are not represented; values before 1970 are not accepted by the Worker API.

methods.title: Caller-supplied Unix nanoseconds
inputs: signed integer nanoseconds from the caller
limitations: Accepted only within 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 UTC.

methods.title: Unix nanoseconds to proleptic Gregorian UTC
methods.source: civil-from-days integer algorithm (proleptic Gregorian), std only
methods.uncertainty: exact representation of the input; inherits the input's uncertainty
limitations: Leap seconds are not representable (no 23:59:60).
Years 0001 to 9999 only.
Not TAI, TT or TDB.

methods.title: Selected Hemant reference epoch
inputs: 1979-01-14 13:29 IST (07:59 UTC), Kashi Makar Sankranti, as selected by the user
methods.source: user selection recorded in hemant-core; no independent citation yet
methods.frame_or_location: Kashi (Varanasi), as described; no coordinates recorded
methods.uncertainty: minute precision; exact astronomical Sankranti instant not established
limitations: Not an astronomical calculation of the Sankranti instant.
A calendar reference, not a clock source.

methods.title: Hemant traditional time units
methods.source: named convention: 30 muhurta/ahoratra, 30 kala/muhurta, 30 kastha/kala, 15 nimesha/kastha
methods.output_units: signed ahoratra + muhurta, kala, kastha, nimesha; residual in nanoseconds
methods.uncertainty: arithmetic is exact under the convention; whole-nimesha flooring residual is reported
limitations: Elapsed duration is a Unix-time difference: leap seconds since the epoch are not counted.
One convention among several traditions; not asserted as universal.

methods.title: JPL Horizons geocentric apparent Sun and Moon angles
methods.source: NASA/JPL Horizons API; runtime response includes provider metadata and ephemeris identity
methods.time_scale: UTC request; Horizons observer ephemeris time handling
methods.frame_or_location: Earth geocenter; apparent ecliptic and equinox of date
methods.uncertainty: not independently quantified; displayed decimal precision is not an uncertainty bound
limitations: Only Sun and Moon angles are returned.
Single provider; no independent ephemeris comparison.
Not spacecraft navigation or an onboard clock.

methods.title: Instantaneous tithi, paksha and karana angle bins
methods.source: integer-microdegree angle arithmetic in hemant-core; 12-degree tithi and 6-degree karana bins
methods.time_scale: input instant supplied in UTC to Horizons
methods.frame_or_location: geocentric apparent ecliptic/equinox of date; no local sunrise assignment
methods.output_units: elongation degrees, ordinal tithi, paksha, karana index and name
methods.uncertainty: inherited from ephemeris and input time; not quantified by this method
limitations: Instant classification only; no civil-day assignment.
Tradition-specific named labels require independent Panchanga test vectors.
Nakshatra and yoga require a selected ayanamsha and are not emitted.

methods.title: Explicit-ayanamsha tithi, nakshatra and yoga angle bins
inputs: same-frame apparent ecliptic Sun/Moon longitudes in microdegrees
methods.source: integer angle-bin arithmetic in hemant-core; 12-degree tithi and exact rational 27-part nakshatra/yoga bins
methods.frame_or_location: caller-supplied apparent ecliptic longitudes; no local sunrise assignment
methods.output_units: one-based tithi, nakshatra and yoga ordinals; integer microdegrees
methods.uncertainty: not calculated; inherited from angle provider, timestamp and selected ayanamsha
limitations: Ayanamsha is required input and has no default.
Arithmetic classifies supplied angles; it does not compute ephemerides.
No tradition-specific names, day assignment, independent comparison, or scientific qualification.

methods.title: Mars 2020 SCLK refit V19 first two intervals demonstration
inputs: decoded first two Type 1 correlation intervals
methods.source: NAIF PDS m2020_168_sclkscet_refit_v19.tsc; pinned two-row subset only
methods.time_scale: TDT seconds past J2000; no UTC or TDB conversion emitted
methods.output_units: integer nanoseconds past J2000 in TDT
methods.uncertainty: inherited from archival clock correlation; not quantified by this subset
limitations: Archival refit explicitly says it was not used during operations.
Only the first two correlation intervals are embedded; all other readings fail closed.
Not a complete NAIF SPICE implementation or a flight-qualified adapter.
UTC conversion needs a leap-seconds kernel; TDT is retained to avoid an unstated conversion.

methods.title: Solar-system positions (ephemeris)
limitations: No ephemeris dataset or library is bundled locally.
A separate JPL Horizons adapter supplies only geocentric apparent Sun/Moon angles.
No wider planetary state vectors are produced by this method.

methods.title: Panchanga ruleset
limitations: Instant tithi/paksha/karana angle bins are exposed by a separate narrow method.
No complete sunrise-assigned Panchanga ruleset is selected.
Nakshatra and yoga need an explicit ayanamsha; other fields need location and calendar rules.
